quality.notes: Three EV fleets (464 vehicles). Each pickle is one 128-row charging segment as an unlabelled 8-column matrix plus a meta record (label, car, charge_segment, mileage, capacity); the columns are recorded as col0..col7. The registry's 'source' column points at the KIT dataset by mistake; its source_url (Mendeley, Tsinghua EV fleets) matches the data. Charging profile: field data from three vehicle types; the channels are unlabelled, so the C-rate is not computed, but the current level differs by an order of magnitude between segments and vehicles. The landing page states 464 EVs of 3 types; the vehicle or battery type of each vehicle is not given there. The paper that releases this dataset is Lu et al., eTransportation 22 (2024) 100361 (Towards real-world state of health estimation, Part 2; full text read). It states: 464 EVs of three types (217, 198 and 49, matching the three archives), all with NCM-C battery material and rated capacities of 145, 155 and 153 Ah (A and B commercial, C private), sampling intervals of 30 s, 10 s and 10 s (dataset 1 interpolated to 10 s), collection periods of 2.2, 1.0 and 2.5 years, and 629,121, 472,829 and 176,327 charging snippets. Each snippet has 128 records of eight series (current, average cell voltage, maximum and minimum cell voltage, highest and lowest cell temperature, SOC, time) plus vehicle number, mileage and regional charged capacity. Charging current is negative. To protect privacy the current, average cell voltage and temperature were perturbed and interpolated and the timestamps and mileage randomly shifted and scaled, so the values are not the original measurements. The paper does not give the column order of the released pickles; the order used here (col0 average cell voltage, col1 current, col2 SOC, col3 maximum and col4 minimum cell voltage, col5 highest and col6 lowest cell temperature, col7 time in seconds) is read from the value ranges. 'NCM-C' is taken as an NMC cathode; the anode is not named, so it stays null. Pack voltage and the number of cells are not given. The paper cites the dataset as Mendeley Data V2 (10.17632/mcsh4hnb8b.2); this record carries the version-1 DOI.
